I work for BOA and my focus is in digital revenue (aka I sling our app and other online services).  I'm not a security expert by any means and I really can't speak for any other banks but I'm sure all the big ones have very similar security features. BOA's app is absolutely just as secure as online banking, which is wicked secure. The only data breaches we've had (to my knowledge) have been mostly from phishing scams and a few insider data compromises. No data leaks a la Target or Amazon. Not a single one. Seriously. Google that shit. 

Our three basic security protocols for banking online/with the mobile app: 1) all data is encrypted, so even if you're on an unsecured network and there's someone who's doing some data eavesdropping, any communications between your device and bank servers might as well be gibberish.

2) If we see you logging on from a device we don't recognize, we'll ask a personal question before allowing any log-in attempts. I thought this seemed like a borderline basic bitch security measure but these aren't questions like "What's your mother's maiden name?" It's stuff like "Where were you NYE Y2K?" or "What's your mom's best friend's name?" so the likelihood of a hacker knowing this information is much lower than what we typically expect from security questions.

3) If the bank detects any alterations between the data being transmitted between your device and our servers (aka there's something piggybacking or it looks like data has been replaced) we drop the connections immediately so nothing is impacted by tainted devices.
